title: TypeScript SDK: composable stream conversion operators and retry orchestration
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a small library of composable conversion operators and orchestration primitives for the TypeScript SDK to make AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams ergonomic, cancel-safe, and retry-friendly. This ticket focuses on operator ergonomics (map/filter/flatMap), safe cancellation propagation (AbortSignal), backpressure preservation, and retry orchestration for resumable stream sources (HTTP fetch + reconnect semantics).
acceptance_criteria: Well-documented TypeScript operators: asyncIteratorToReadableStream, readableStreamToAsyncIterator, mapAsync, filterAsync, takeWhile, withRetryableReconnect
Operators correctly propagate AbortSignal and preserve backpressure in Node + browser runtimes
Retry orchestration supports idempotency tokens and resumes at chunk boundaries for reconnect-capable sources
Unit and integration tests demonstrating retry/fallback and cancellation interactions
Examples added to SDK examples folder showing patterns: consumer-first AsyncIterator apps, Web Stream piping in browser, and server-side pipeline with transform operators
API surface reviewed with SDK ergonomics team and documentation merged
technical_notes: Goals: make conversions explicit and composable, avoid hidden buffering that breaks latency SLOs, and provide primitives that make building resilient consumers straightforward.

Design constraints: must work in Node 18+ (native web streams) and browsers; avoid any runtime-only dependencies; implement in TS with narrow runtime checks for global ReadableStream/ReadableStreamDefaultReader availability.

Cancellation: all APIs accept an optional AbortSignal. Conversions must forward the signal to underlying readers/writers and close/throw consistently so callers can distinguish cancellation vs. upstream error.

Backpressure: when converting AsyncIterator -> ReadableStream, pull() should only request from iterator when sink is ready. When converting ReadableStream -> AsyncIterator, chunk pulls must await reader.read() and yield in order; do not buffer more than 1 chunk by default unless user opts in.

Retries: provide withRetryableReconnect(operatorOpts) which wraps a source factory (() => { stream, resumeToken? }) and handles reconnect attempts, resume handshake, and backoff. Resume tokens are opaque strings produced by servers or by K/V cache based on last-seen chunk index.
Idempotency: recommend callers provide an idempotencyKey when retrying POST-based streaming endpoints. SDK will attach header X-Redwood-Idempotency if provided.
Streaming framing: support both length-prefixed and newline-delimited JSON streams. Provide a framing helper that yields complete JSON objects and exposes lastCompleteOffset for resume tokens.
Edge cases: streaming JSON fragments, binary payloads, simultaneous consumer detach + reconnect, and partially-consumed buffers must be handled deterministically.
Security: do not persist resume tokens in cleartext in logs. Document that resume tokens may contain offsets and recommend encryption in enterprise flows. Flag security_review_required below.
implementation_tasks: Create core conversion primitives: asyncIteratorToReadableStream(src, opts?), readableStreamToAsyncIterator(stream, opts?)
Implement operator helpers: mapAsync(fn), filterAsync(pred), flatMapAsync(mapper), take(n), takeWhile(pred)
Implement framing utilities: ndjsonFramer(), lengthPrefixFramer() that return async iterators of parsed messages plus lastOffset metadata
Build withRetryableReconnect(sourceFactory, opts) orchestration primitive with exponential backoff and jitter, abort propagation, and idempotency header support
Add TypeScript declarations, runtime checks, and small polyfill helpers for older Node runtimes
Write unit tests for conversions, operators, and framing in JSDOM + Node test runners
Add integration test that spins up a local streaming HTTP server which supports resume tokens to validate reconnect semantics
Docs: write SDK usage guide and three examples (consumer-async-iterator, browser-pipe, server-transform-pipeline)
API review with DX team, iterate on naming and ergonomics
tests: Unit: conversion primitives under normal flow, cancellation, and thrown errors
Unit: operator composition mapAsync -> filterAsync -> takeWhile ensuring no extra buffering
Integration: simulated flaky HTTP stream that drops connection every N chunks, verify withRetryableReconnect resumes and yields all messages in order
Browser: example mounting of readable stream to <div> via stream.pipeTo(new WritableStream(...)) with backpressure observed
Performance: microbenchmarks comparing conversion with and without an explicit small buffer (1-4 chunks) to validate latency impact
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag 'ts-stream-interop' for a canary release. Publish beta on npm under @redwood-inference/sdk-next with clear migration doc. Monitor consumer telemetry (latency, rebuffer events, reconnects) for two weeks before enabling default for new app templates.
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created. Drafted goals and acceptance criteria. Marked as P1 because this unblocks multiple customer patterns for retries and lower-level SDK ergonomics.

2025-02-17 Arjun Patel: Spike complete—validated that Node native Web Streams + browser ReadableStream interop works with a 0-buffer approach. Observed a 9% latency win vs naive buffering but had more frequent micro stalls under high concurrency. Proposed optional smallBuffer param.

2025-02-19 Design review (Lena Ortiz): Prefer explicit operator names over magic 'pipe' variants. Suggested mapAsync / filterAsync to match existing SDK style. Also requested small code examples for docs.

2025-02-21 Security (Ibrahim Khan): Noted that resume tokens may leak offsets. Request added: document recommended encryption and add no-logging policy for resume tokens. Marked security_review_required.
2025-02-24 Arjun Patel: Implemented basic framing helpers and ndjson framer. Integration test for flaky server working locally. Still iterating on resume token shape with backend team (PM-408).
2025-02-26 Maya Chen: API review scheduled for 2025-03-03. Preparing examples and a short migration guide.
